title: Stratified runtime orchestrator for phasewise kernel exploration and prefill-aware scheduling
creator: Aisha R. Patel
description:
Background: Our serving runtime currently picks kernels primarily via static heuristics and occasional warmstarts. This yields suboptimal choices across heterogeneous hardware and mixed sequence length traffic, especially for workloads that flip between long prefill batches and short decode bursts. Goal: build a stratified runtime orchestrator that explores kernel variants phasewise (prefill vs decode) with hysteresis to avoid flapping, uses lightweight architecture fingerprints and seqlen bucketing, and learns a cost-latency model online to recommend warmstarts and fallback policies.

Scope: design and implement a runtime component that: (1) classifies incoming requests into phase groups (prefill, decode, mixed), (2) maintains per-arch, per-seqlen histogram state and a small probe budget, (3) runs controlled micro-probes to evaluate rarely-used but potentially better kernels (e.g., blockwise-attn, fused-attn, flash variants, quantized paths), (4) incorporates a hysteresis window so the system does not oscillate on transient changes, (5) exposes knobs for canary/cost-safety envelopes and operator overrides.

Key ideas: stratified state (arch: gpu family, mem topology, chiplet; seqlen buckets: short<64, mid 64-512, long>512; batch size buckets), phasewise heuristics (separate probes for prefill vs decode), lightweight online cost model (exponential moving averages for p50/p95 latency and tokens/sec, plus compute cost proxy), probe scheduling (budgeted sampling using Thompson-like exploration with safety guardrails), and graceful fallbacks when probes show regression beyond safety thresholds.

Telemetry & metrics: add events for probe_start/probe_end, kernel_choice, kernel_fallback, phase_transition, hysteresis_state. Track p50/p95 latency, tail latency >=99.9, throughput (tokens/sec), per-token cost estimate, and probe success rate.

Why this is different: instead of a single global kernel autotuner, this approach maintains stratified local models keyed by architecture and token-phase. The hysteresis and phase-awareness are intended to reduce noisy switching and to respect differing SLOs between prefill (throughput-oriented) and decode (latency-oriented).

Non-goals: global model training, long-running offline model fitters, and heavy-weight per-request profiling that increases latency.

Risks & mitigations: (1) Probe overhead causing latency regressions -> limit probe budget and run probes on warm idle GPUs or use low-priority lanes. (2) State explosion across many arch/seqlen combos -> compress histograms, cap combinations, and evict cold keys. (3) Incorrect microbenchmarks vs real traffic -> include shadowing and replay tests before canary.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime implements per-arch + seqlen bucket state and classifies request phase (prefill/decode)
Probe mechanism that can exercise at least 3 kernel variants non-disruptively and record latency/cost metrics
Hysteresis logic in place that prevents kernel flips for at least N=30s or configurable window
Automated safety checks that abort probe-driven rollouts when p95 increases by >10% or token-cost increases by >8%
End-to-end infra tests and a canary rollout demonstrating improved p95 or cost-per-token for at least one production workload
Perf dashboard widgets for probe success rate, kernel choice distribution, and phasewise resource utilization
plan: Week 1: design API + telemetry schema; align on seqlen buckets and arch fingerprint fields
Week 2: implement lightweight state store and phase classifier; add probe scheduler interface
Week 3: integrate two new kernel variants (blockwise-attn, fused-attn) into probe harness; unit + microbenchmarks
Week 4: safety checks, hysteresis engine, and dashboard plumbing
Week 5: shadow tests with sampled traffic; run replay against historical workloads
Week 6: canary rollout to low-traffic shard; measure and iterate; prepare roll-forward or rollback plan
experiments: Microbench A: short-prefill workload on A100 and RTX-6000 with batch sizes 1,4,16 — compare fused vs flash-attn
Microbench B: decode-heavy (single token) latency test across seqlen buckets — measure tail latencies
Probe budget sweep: evaluate 0.1%, 1%, 5% probe traffic and impact on stability
Hysteresis window ablation: 5s vs 30s vs 120s, measure flip frequency and SLO violations
Eviction policy test: cap of 100 stratified keys vs 500 and measure memory + cold-miss rate
rollout: Stage 0: internal dev cluster with synthetic workloads
Stage 1: shadow mode in production for 72 hours, no rollbacks applied automatically
Stage 2: canary to 3% of traffic for 48 hours with strict p95/p99 guardrails
Stage 3: ramp to 25% and monitor cost and latency metrics; if stable, expand to 100%
Rollback: immediate disable and fallback to baseline kernel if safety checks fire
notes: Decision: use 3 seqlen buckets (short/mid/long) for initial rollout to limit state cardinality
Trade-off: favor faster probes for decode phase and more aggressive exploration for prefill phase where throughput gains outweigh occasional latency blips
